fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance that is visible from both directions of the approaching road.

• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to reach the main residence without obstruction.

• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive so vehicles can pass without branches blocking the path or reducing visibility.

• Mark the detached structure with a visible identifier so responders can locate it quickly without searching the property.

• Keep a gate or opening at the rear of the property unlocked or clearly marked to give responders an alternate route if the front access drive is blocked.

• Cut back dense vegetation along the sides of the access drive to maintain clear sightlines for approaching responders and to allow two personnel to walk alongside a vehicle if needed.

• Identify a flat, open area near the front of the property where emergency vehicles can turn around, and keep it clear of stored equipment, vehicles, and debris.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Grass Cover; Open Terrain; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Long Driveway; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim any shrubs that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls or foundation.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their branches do not touch the roof or each other.
• Keep grass mowed short around the house, especially during dry months.
• Clear any dead grass or dry plant material that has accumulated against the base of the house.
• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches along its full length so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate quickly, particularly if the route is not well signed from the road.
• Keep the single access route free of parked vehicles, stored materials, or other obstructions that could slow entry or exit during an emergency.
